channel.title: Palm Coast Observer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Palm Coast Observer (observerlocalnews.com)

item.title: Flagler County begins conflict resolution process with Flagler Beach over Summertown development
item.description: Despite the formality of the proceedings, both parties felt the issues could be resolved outside of a lawsuit.

item.title: End of an era: Class of 2026 says farewell to Harry Wendelstedt Umpire School after 50 years
item.description: Following Major League Baseball's decision to take over umpire training, the class of 2026 will be the last class to graduate at the Ormond Beach school.

item.title: Palm Coast, Flagler County lean toward $2.1 million animal shelter, need input from other cities
item.description: Despite the ongoing research conducted by the a task force, many decisions are contingent to answers the boards do not have yet. The shelter will ultimately be run by a nonprofit.

item.title: Florida House panel approves major health care bill
item.description: The wide-ranging plan seeks to trim health-care regulations and carry out federal changes in food stamps and Medicaid.

item.title: Florida weekly jobless claims dip
item.description: An estimate 5,540 unemployment claims were filed last week, down from 6,546 the previous week.

item.title: Daytona Beach man arrested for firing gun inside Bunnell bar to pop a balloon
item.description: Richard William Graham, 73, was arrested during a traffic stop on Jan. 23, 20 days after the incident occurred. He is a known affiliate of the Outlaws motorcycle gang, a press release said.

item.title: Palm Coast-Flagler Regional Chamber of Commerce presents 2026 awards at its annual meeting
item.description: Award winners were: David Ayers, Donna McGevna, Lauren Johnston, Advent Health — Denyse Bales-Chubb and Quantum Electrical Contractors — Joe Wright.

item.title: Four theft suspects in unrelated cases arrested between Jan. 27-29
item.description: Three suspects were arrested by the Flagler County Sheriff's Office and the fourth by the St. Johns County Sheriff's Office.

item.title: Buddy Taylor Middle School students step into their future at Career Expo
item.description: Matanzas and Flagler Palm Coast students discussed their programs of study and local businesses, governments and nonprofits showcased a variety of career paths.

item.title: Holland Financial CEO donates over 800 copies of new book to the Volusia Sheriff's Office
item.description: The recent "Thank the Blue" donation event at the VSO Training Center was held in appreciation for local law enforcement.
